title: Pareto Concentration and ABC Classification
description: Quantifying concentration of revenue, inventory, or activity among top entities using the 80/20 principle.
conditions: Assessing revenue dependency on top accounts, product concentration, or clinical workload distribution
Need to establish tiered operational service levels
recommended_methods: Cumulative percentage Pareto curve and Gini concentration coefficient
ABC Stratification (A: Top 80% value from ~20% entities, B: Next 15% value, C: Tail 5% value)
Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) for market concentration measurement
selection_rules: Classify entities into Tier A (80% cumulative value), Tier B (next 15%), and Tier C (bottom 5%)
If Gini coefficient > 0.75 or top 5% accounts generate > 60% revenue, flag severe revenue concentration risk
Tailor retention workflows: Tier A accounts require dedicated human management; Tier C accounts use automated workflows
limitations: Heavy focus on Tier A can neglect high-growth Tier C accounts with massive expansion potential
Concentration metrics describe static snapshot states and do not predict account migration trajectories
